items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: That was the church founded by Richard Allen. He was one of the first black bishops in the Methodist Conference, and he had a church down at Sixth and Lombard.

ctx.x: But they only said -- and there was only one thing that was going to happen to me for playing ragtime -- you'd end up with consumption, tuberculosis, or you'd end up in somebody's penitentiary. So, for being too smart. So they said -- after they found that I was going to play the music, anyhow, they said, maybe

"Well, let's give him a good musical education so that he can play on the church choir," Cause we were all members of Bethel AME Church. That was the church founded by Richard Allen. He was one of the first black bishops in the Methodist Conference, and he had a church down at Sixth and Lombard. Well, we used to go down there every Sunday. And we'd play around there and even go down around his tomb. They've got him buried in there.

But I didn't think much of that, because, on the corner was a saloon. And while these people'd be in there playing, all like that, another crowd was hanging in the saloon, and the man -- the church couldn't move him because, at every rally, he gave the church $50.00 or $100.00, so he went on down there so, right from the beginning I wasn't so for religion anyhow. But I tried to get it, but I got out there and they shouted over me, and stomped and dust and stuff up, but it didn't work.
